sentences.2: He's always so crude and impolite.
sentences.3: When the wedding comes, expect him to smash the cake.

leftover: 'expect' as an instruction to the listener
that the cake ends up smashed: a change of state, which the rulebook has no result for
translator's readings: 'That' in sentence 4 read as smashing the cake; 'at weddings' added to the habit

2.text: [CLAIMED] Markus is ALWAYS crude and impolite

4.text: [CLAIMED] Markus will smash the cake at the wedding

5.text: [CLAIMED] Markus USUALLY smashes the cake at weddings (a habit: it SHOWS, it does not MAKE)

6.text: expect him to smash the cake SINCE it is a wedding and that is his habit

7.text: expect him to smash the cake SINCE he is always crude and impolite
